tweets.content:
Press club's @PCITweets clear statement was welcomed. Particularly concerning over the @Outlookindia Magazine's journalist who "was fired upon by weapon resembling a pellet gun".

Press Club of India (@PCITweets)

The Press Club of India condemns the recent attacks on and violence against journalists who are covering the youth protests in New Delhi.

We have also seen with particular concern @Outlookindia Magazine's report that one of their journalists was fired upon by a weapon resembling a pellet gun and has severely injured his arm.

At least three other such instances of pellet-like injuries have also been reported.

We urge the police and security personnel, and those gathered to ensure their safety.

We also call upon the government to restore mobile internet services in the area at this crucial time.

tweets.title: RT by @NetramDefence: The Indian Army has formally begun raising its first five Integrated Battle Groups (IBGs) and a Fire Support Group under the 17 Mountain Strike Corps in the Eastern Command, enhancing rapid-response capabilities along the China front. Each IBG is a self-contained, combined-arms formation of around 5,000 personnel, integrating infantry, armour, artillery, air defence, engineers and logistics. Designed for deployment within 12–48 hours, the formations are tailored to the Threat, Terrain and Task of each operational sector. Originally conceived with Pakistan in mind, the first IBGs have instead been deployed opposite China in Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim, reflecting India's evolving security priorities following the 2020 LAC standoff. Military analysts view the IBGs as the institutional realization, and modernization, of India's long-discussed "Cold Start" concept, providing New Delhi with a credible option for rapid, limited conventional responses below the threshold of prolonged mobilization.
tweets.content:
The Indian Army has formally begun raising its first five Integrated Battle Groups (IBGs) and a Fire Support Group under the 17 Mountain Strike Corps in the Eastern Command, enhancing rapid-response capabilities along the China front.

Each IBG is a self-contained, combined-arms formation of around 5,000 personnel, integrating infantry, armour, artillery, air defence, engineers and logistics. Designed for deployment within 12–48 hours, the formations are tailored to the Threat, Terrain and Task of each operational sector.

Originally conceived with Pakistan in mind, the first IBGs have instead been deployed opposite China in Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim, reflecting India's evolving security priorities following the 2020 LAC standoff.

Military analysts view the IBGs as the institutional realization, and modernization, of India's long-discussed "Cold Start" concept, providing New Delhi with a credible option for rapid, limited conventional responses below the threshold of prolonged mobilization.
